fullAnalysis: Puzzle #752 opens with Motor, Damage, Quality, Remote, and Air traffic, a set of clues that appear to belong to completely different categories on first read. That spread is what makes the board deceptive: instead of pointing toward a single subject area, the clues push you toward toys, brands, folklore, or everyday vocabulary all at once. When Pinpoint does this, the safer move is to stop grouping by topic and start testing whether the same missing word can complete every clue naturally.

That approach resolves this board quickly. The shared connector is "control". Once you test "control" across the full list, each phrase settles into a clean compound and the noise disappears. The answer "Words that come before "control"" works because it explains every clue with the same exact pattern, not because one or two clues feel loosely related. If one connector completes all five without stretching the meaning, that is usually the correct Pinpoint solution.
